questions.question: At the end of the language skills topic, students should be able to define which term?
questions.explanation: One of the stated learning objectives is to define the term language skills.

questions.question: The learning objectives of language skills include listing which of the following?
questions.explanation: Students should be able to list the types of language skills.

questions.question: The learning objectives require students to differentiate between listening and which other skill?
questions.explanation: One objective is to differentiate between listening and speaking.

questions.question: Students are expected to differentiate between reading and which other skill?
questions.explanation: One objective is to differentiate between reading and writing.

questions.question: Reading skill deals with the ability to perceive and understand which type of symbols?
questions.explanation: Reading skill deals with the ability to perceive and understand writing symbols.

questions.question: In reading, textual elements such as letters are combined to form which units?
questions.explanation: Letters are combined to form words, phrases, clauses and sentences.

questions.question: In the reading process, the writer is regarded as which of the following?
questions.explanation: The writer is regarded as the encoder who ties up the message.

questions.question: In the reading process, the reader is referred to as which of the following?
questions.explanation: The reader is referred to as the decoder who reads and interprets the message.

questions.question: The writer writes using which type of signs and symbols?
questions.explanation: The writer writes using graphological signs and symbols.

questions.question: The ability to understand the relationship between words and phrases, phrases and clauses, and clauses and sentences is considered which type of ability?
questions.explanation: This is listed as one of the reading abilities.

questions.question: Which of the following is listed as a purpose of reading?
questions.explanation: Reading serves the purpose of getting information.

questions.question: Obtaining guidance is classified as which aspect of reading?
questions.explanation: Obtaining guidance is one of the purposes of reading.

questions.question: Reading for relaxation is classified under which category?
questions.explanation: Relaxation is listed as one of the purposes of reading.

questions.question: Development of intellectual ability is listed as which of the following?
questions.explanation: Development of intellectual ability is one of the purposes of reading.

questions.question: Reading without audible noise is known by which term?
questions.explanation: Silent reading is reading without audible noise and is the most appropriate type.

questions.question: Reading with audible noise is particularly used during which activity?
questions.explanation: Reading aloud is particularly used during speech presentation.

questions.question: Reading to target or solve a particular problem is called which type of reading?
questions.explanation: Creative reading is reading to target or solve a particular problem.

questions.question: Reading to react positively or negatively to a topic depending on meaning is called which type of reading?
questions.explanation: Critical reading involves reacting to what is good or bad based on the meaning from the passage.

questions.question: Reading to get specific detailed information is known by which type?
questions.explanation: Intensive reading is reading to get specific detailed information.

questions.question: Intensive reading is also known by which alternative name?
questions.explanation: Intensive reading is also known as slow-careful reading, used for difficult text.

questions.question: The habit of pronouncing each word aloud as you read is called which term?
questions.explanation: Vocalisation refers to the habit of pronouncing each word aloud as you read.

questions.question: Sub-vocalisation refers to pronouncing each word in which manner?
questions.explanation: Sub-vocalisation involves pronouncing each word within your mind or hearing yourself as you read.

questions.question: Counting a number of words before reading is considered which of the following?
questions.explanation: Counting words is a bad habit that slows reading speed.

questions.question: Using a biro or finger to track the line as you read is called which practice?
questions.explanation: Finger pointing is using a biro or finger to track the line and is a practice used by children.

questions.question: Moving your head from side to side when reading is called which practice?
questions.explanation: Head movement is a practice of moving your head from side to side when reading.

questions.question: Thinking of irrelevant things not related to the reading is called which practice?
questions.explanation: Daydreaming involves thinking of other irrelevant things during reading.

questions.question: The ability of reading with the aim of storing what you have read is called which term?
questions.explanation: Memorisation is reading with the aim of storing what has been read.

questions.question: Memorisation is considered a bad form of reading because it carries the danger of inability to do which of the following?
questions.explanation: Memorisation risks inability to recall due to psychological tension, especially during examinations.

questions.question: To break the habit of daydreaming during reading, you should always have what for your reading?
questions.explanation: Having a purpose for reading helps break the habit of daydreaming.

questions.question: Making notes as you read helps you to do which of the following?
questions.explanation: Making notes as you read helps you concentrate very well.

questions.question: Writing skill is defined as the act of expressing ideas through which medium?
questions.explanation: Writing skill is the act of expressing ideas through written words.

questions.question: Ogayi (2005) defines writing skill as the skillful use of language symbols to express thoughts on which surface?
questions.explanation: Writing involves using language symbols to express thoughts on paper or any other writing surface.

questions.question: Writing is a complex exercise that starts from the ability to recognize letters of which element?
questions.explanation: Writing starts from recognizing letters of the alphabet to spelling of words.

questions.question: According to Ogayi (2005), the writer needs to organize his pieces of information or ideas in which structure?
questions.explanation: The writer needs to organize information or ideas in paragraphs.

questions.question: Writing is described as a very complex exercise that begins with which ability?
questions.explanation: Writing begins with the ability to recognize letters of the alphabet before moving to sentence construction.

questions.question: Before constructing compound and complex sentences, the learner must first master which skill?
questions.explanation: Elementary sentence making comes before constructing compound, complex and multiple constructions.

questions.question: Reading extensively, intensively and regularly helps improve writing skill because it exposes the reader to which elements?
questions.explanation: As you read, you come across new vocabularies and good presentations that improve writing.

questions.question: Writing with your audience in mind helps determine whether you should write in which style?
questions.explanation: The audience determines whether to use formal or informal style.

questions.question: It is wrong to use informal words when writing a document meant for which matters?
questions.explanation: Using informal words for official documents is considered wrong.

questions.question: It is wrong to use formal words when writing to people who are which type?
questions.explanation: Using formal words with less educated people is considered wrong.

questions.question: Knowledge of written convention requires you to set out an appropriate what when you write?
questions.explanation: You should be able to set out an appropriate tone when you write.

questions.question: It is advisable to write when you are less angry to enable you to communicate in which manner?
questions.explanation: Writing when less angry helps communicate with an appropriate tone.

questions.question: Reading your writing aloud helps in drawing your attention particularly to which aspects?
questions.explanation: Reading aloud helps draw attention to areas where there are errors.

questions.question: Reading aloud after writing helps you to do away with wrong grammar and which other elements?
questions.explanation: Reading aloud helps eliminate wrong grammar and punctuation marks.

questions.question: Maintaining different sentence types helps to improve writing skills by combining simple, compound, complex and which other type?
questions.explanation: A good knowledge of simple, compound, complex, compound complex and multiple sentence types helps improve writing.

questions.question: Using only one sentence variety in writing sounds which way?
questions.explanation: Using only one variety type in writing sounds monotonous.

questions.question: Combining different types of sentences helps maintain good rhythm and creates what type of flow?
questions.explanation: Combining different sentence types creates a natural flow.

questions.question: Unity and cohesion requires that every other element in the work contributes to which idea?
questions.explanation: Every element in the work should contribute to one central idea.

questions.question: To improve writing, every idea should be linked to which element in the work?
questions.explanation: Every idea should be linked to the central idea in the work.

questions.question: The ability to recognize the letters of the alphabet is listed as which type of ability in reading?
questions.explanation: Recognizing letters is listed as one of the reading abilities.
